description: Hard veto list. FortressOne will refuse to disable or remove anything listed here, regardless of tier or user selection. Every entry states WHY. If you disagree with an entry, the answer is to edit this file deliberately, not to have the tool guess.
_note_on_philosophy: The purpose of a debloat tool is to remove things that cost you performance. Nothing on this list costs meaningful performance in a Fortnite session, and every item on it breaks either the game, the controller, the network, or the ability to boot. Removing them is not 'more aggressive optimisation' — it is breakage with no upside.

services.name: EasyAntiCheat
services.reason: Fortnite will not launch without Easy Anti-Cheat. Non-negotiable.

services.name: EasyAntiCheat_EOS
services.reason: Epic Online Services anti-cheat driver used by current Fortnite builds.

services.name: BEService
services.reason: BattlEye. Fortnite ships both anti-cheats; disabling either can block launch.

services.name: Audiosrv
services.reason: Windows Audio. No game audio, and no positional audio cues, without it.

services.name: AudioEndpointBuilder
services.reason: Enumerates audio devices. Disabling silences the machine entirely.

services.name: hidserv
services.reason: Human Interface Device service. Your GameSir controller is an HID device — this is the controller stack.

services.name: HidUsb
services.reason: USB HID driver. Directly required for a wired controller to enumerate.

services.name: xusb22
services.reason: Xbox 360/XInput controller driver. Your GameSir runs in Xbox layout, which means XInput, which means this driver.

services.name: xboxgip
services.reason: Xbox Game Input Protocol driver — used by Xbox-layout controllers over USB.

services.name: USBXHCI
services.reason: USB 3.x host controller driver. Removing it disconnects every USB device including your controller.

services.name: usbhub
services.reason: USB hub driver. Same consequence as above.

services.name: nsi
services.reason: Network Store Interface. Disabling this breaks all networking, immediately and completely.

services.name: BFE
services.reason: Base Filtering Engine. Windows drops all network traffic without it. A classic 'my internet died after debloating' cause.

services.name: Dhcp
services.reason: Required to obtain an IP address from your router.

services.name: Dnscache
services.reason: DNS client. Disabling forces uncached lookups and raises, not lowers, connection latency.

services.name: NlaSvc
services.reason: Network Location Awareness. Windows firewall profile and connectivity detection depend on it.

services.name: netprofm
services.reason: Network List Service. NlaSvc depends on it.

services.name: TCPIP
services.reason: The TCP/IP stack itself.

services.name: Netbt
services.reason: NetBIOS over TCP/IP; part of the core stack binding.

services.name: CryptSvc
services.reason: Cryptographic Services. Certificate validation for Epic login, EAC handshake and Windows Update all fail without it.

services.name: RpcSs
services.reason: Remote Procedure Call. The majority of Windows is built on it. Disabling prevents boot.

services.name: DcomLaunch
services.reason: DCOM Server Process Launcher. Disabling prevents boot.

services.name: RpcEptMapper
services.reason: RPC Endpoint Mapper. Disabling prevents boot.

services.name: PlugPlay
services.reason: Plug and Play. Device enumeration, including your controller and GPU.

services.name: Power
services.reason: Power service. Required for the power plan and CPU state control this tool configures.

services.name: Winmgmt
services.reason: WMI. Hardware monitoring, GPU driver components and this tool's own diagnostics depend on it.

services.name: gpsvc
services.reason: Group Policy Client. Disabling causes login failure on many systems.

services.name: ProfSvc
services.reason: User Profile Service. Disabling means you cannot log in.

services.name: UserManager
services.reason: Required for user session initialisation.

services.name: Schedule
services.reason: Task Scheduler. Windows uses it for servicing and maintenance; disabling causes broad, hard-to-diagnose breakage.

services.name: SystemEventsBroker
services.reason: Core broker; many services fail to start without it.

services.name: CoreMessagingRegistrar
services.reason: Core messaging. Disabling causes boot failure on Windows 11.

services.name: TrustedInstaller
services.reason: Windows Modules Installer. Required to service or repair Windows later.

services.name: msiserver
services.reason: Windows Installer. Required to install or repair the game, GPU driver, or runtimes.

services.name: nvlddmkm
services.reason: NVIDIA display driver kernel module.

services.name: NVDisplay.ContainerLocalSystem
services.reason: NVIDIA display container. Removing it breaks NVIDIA Control Panel and the driver-side Reflex/low-latency settings this tool configures.

services.name: nvagent
services.reason: NVIDIA network service component used by the driver stack.

services.name: StorSvc
services.reason: Storage service.

services.name: volmgr
services.reason: Volume manager. Boot-critical storage driver.

services.name: partmgr
services.reason: Partition manager. Boot-critical storage driver.

services.name: disk
services.reason: Disk class driver. Boot-critical.

services.name: storahci
services.reason: AHCI storage controller driver. Disabling causes an unbootable system (INACCESSIBLE_BOOT_DEVICE).

services.name: stornvme
services.reason: NVMe storage driver. Disabling causes an unbootable system.

services.name: iaStorV
services.reason: Intel RAID/AHCI driver. Boot-critical on Intel chipsets such as your Z590.

services.name: EhStorClass
services.reason: Enhanced storage class driver.

services.name: Winsock
services.reason: Winsock. Sockets, therefore all game networking.

services.name: AFD
services.reason: Ancillary Function Driver for Winsock. The kernel half of every socket the game opens.

services.name: EventLog
services.reason: Windows Event Log. Numerous services declare a hard dependency and fail to start without it.

services.name: SamSs
services.reason: Security Accounts Manager. Disabling prevents boot.

services.name: LSM
services.reason: Local Session Manager. Disabling prevents login.

services.name: Themes
services.reason: Required for correct fullscreen/windowed behaviour and DWM composition on Windows 11.

registryPrefixes.reason: Anti-cheat configuration. Modifying it is both a launch failure and a ban risk.
Safe Mode configuration. This is your recovery path if a tweak goes wrong — it must survive.
Windows setup state. Corruption here can make the machine unbootable and unrepairable.
LSA secrets store. Nothing here is a performance setting.
Account database. Nothing here is a performance setting.

applications.reason: Fortnite and Easy Anti-Cheat link against the VC++ runtimes. Removing these is the single most common cause of 'the game stopped launching after I debloated'.
Used by the Epic Games Launcher and parts of the NVIDIA driver stack.
Fortnite's renderer. Performance Mode is a DirectX 12 path.
Your GPU driver and control panel. This tool configures Reflex and low-latency mode through it.
The entire point of the machine.
Z590 chipset drivers. Removing them degrades PCIe, USB and storage behaviour.
Audio driver. Removing it costs you positional audio, which is a competitive loss, not a gain.
Driver packages. Removal here is how you lose your controller or your NIC.
